terms.means: An interception the defender runs back for a touchdown. About the worst thing a quarterback can do.
terms.use: He stared down his guy and threw a pick-six. Brutal.

terms.means: Inside the other team's 20-yard line, close enough that you should come away with points.
terms.use: We move the ball fine, then we get to the red zone and settle for three.

terms.means: The offense runs three plays, doesn't get a first down, and has to punt. In the CFL, with only three downs, it's a two-and-out.
terms.use: Another three-and-out. Our defense hasn't had a breather all day.

terms.means: CFL only. Two plays, no first down, then a punt on third down. Don't say it about an NFL game.
terms.use: Two-and-out again, and here comes the punter.

terms.means: A long, desperate throw into the end zone as time runs out, hoping someone on your team comes down with it.
terms.use: Nothing left but a Hail Mary. Throw it up and pray.

terms.means: Tackling the quarterback behind the line before he can throw.
terms.use: That's the third sack. Somebody block somebody!

terms.means: Giving the ball to the other team by throwing an interception or losing a fumble.
terms.use: Two turnovers in the first half. You can't win like that.

terms.means: Dropping or losing the ball while carrying it. Either team can pick it up.
terms.use: He was carrying it like a loaf of bread and fumbled. Hold on to the ball!

terms.means: The defense sends extra players, usually linebackers or defensive backs, charging at the quarterback.
terms.use: They blitzed and nobody picked it up. He never had a chance.

terms.means: The quarterback changes the play at the line after seeing how the defense lines up.
terms.use: You could see him audible at the line, and it worked perfectly.

terms.means: The quarterback fakes a handoff to sucker the defense into expecting a run, then throws.
terms.use: Play-action gets them every time. The linebackers bit hard.

terms.means: A short, safe throw, usually to a running back or tight end, when nothing is open downfield.
terms.use: Third and twelve and he throws a checkdown for four yards. Come on.

terms.means: An offense that lives on short passes and rarely throws deep. Usually said as a dig.
terms.use: All this dink and dunk is killing me. Take a shot downfield!

terms.means: A big gain in one go, roughly 20 yards or more.
terms.use: We need some chunk plays. Ten-play drives for a field goal won't cut it.

terms.means: A perfectly placed pass. 'Throwing dimes' means he's on target all day.
terms.use: Did you see that throw? Absolute dime, right over the shoulder.

terms.means: Run all the way for a touchdown, usually on a long run or a return. Also 'he housed it.'
terms.use: He caught it in stride and took it to the house.

terms.means: The end of a lopsided game when the result is settled. Stats from then don't count for much in fans' eyes.
terms.use: Don't get excited about his numbers. Half of that came in garbage time.

terms.means: A defense that gives up yards between the 20s but tightens up and keeps teams out of the end zone.
terms.use: They gave up yards all day, but bend-don't-break, they kept them out of the end zone.

terms.means: A quarterback who avoids mistakes but doesn't win games on his own. Often a backhanded compliment.
terms.use: He's a game manager. Doesn't lose you games, doesn't win you many either.

terms.means: Calling a timeout right before a field-goal try so the kicker has to wait and think about it.
terms.use: They called a timeout to ice the kicker and he nailed it anyway.

terms.means: A short kickoff the kicking team tries to recover itself, usually when it's behind late.
terms.use: They have to try an onside kick here. Get the hands team out there.

terms.means: Slang for the yellow penalty flags the officials throw.
terms.use: There's laundry all over the field. Just let them play!

terms.means: The fight between the offensive and defensive linemen at the line of scrimmage.
terms.use: Games are won in the trenches, and we got beat up front.

terms.means: Picking up first downs and keeping a drive alive. The chains are the sideline markers that measure ten yards.
terms.use: No big plays, but they kept moving the chains and ate up the clock.

terms.means: Someone who second-guesses every call after the game, with hindsight.
terms.use: Easy to Monday morning quarterback it, but that call made no sense.

terms.means: A hurry-up offense at the end of a half, trying to score before the clock runs out.
terms.use: Two minutes, two timeouts. Let's see what he's got in the two-minute drill.

terms.means: Run a play on fourth down to get a first down instead of punting or kicking a field goal.
terms.use: Fourth and inches at midfield? Go for it!

terms.means: The defense stops the other team from scoring a touchdown when they're right at the goal line.
terms.use: Four tries from the one and they didn't get in. What a goal-line stand.

terms.means: Soft, deep coverage used to protect a late lead by stopping big plays. Fans blame it when the other team marches down the field anyway.
terms.use: We went into prevent and they marched right down the field.

terms.means: A physical, run-heavy offense that wears the defense down.
terms.use: Old-school ground and pound. Run it, run it, run it again.

terms.means: The quarterback kneels right after the snap to run out the clock and end the game. Also called the victory formation.
terms.use: They're out of timeouts. Just take a knee and we're done.

terms.means: The one week in the regular season when a team has no game.
terms.use: Good timing for the bye week. Half the roster's banged up.

terms.means: A trick play: handoff to the running back, who pitches it back to the quarterback, who throws deep.
terms.use: They ran a flea flicker and caught the whole secondary napping.

terms.means: CFL only. A single point when a kick ends up in the end zone and the returner doesn't bring it out. Since 2026 there's no single for a missed field goal that goes wide or a kick that leaves the end zone untouched. The NFL has nothing like it.
terms.use: Punt into the end zone, he takes a knee, that's a single. Only in the CFL.

open.m: Works any day after a game. Let them tell you how it went.
Before a game. Gets them talking about the matchup.

open.t: What'd you make of that game?
open.m: Open-ended. They'll fill in the details for you.
Most fans play fantasy football, and they love to complain about it.
Ask before you commit to an opinion. Saves you praising their rival.
Before a home game. A tailgate is the pre-game party in the stadium parking lot.
Every week is a big game to somebody.

opinion.t: It all comes down to the trenches. Win up front, you win the game.
opinion.m: Line play. A safe take about any team.

opinion.t: We have to be more aggressive on fourth down.
opinion.m: Fans almost always want their team to go for it.

opinion.t: Too many penalties. We keep shooting ourselves in the foot.
opinion.m: Penalties are always a fair complaint.

opinion.t: Turnovers will kill you every time.
opinion.m: Giving the ball away loses more games than anything. Hard to argue.

opinion.t: We need to get the ball to our playmakers more.
opinion.m: Every fan thinks their best players should touch it more.

opinion.t: The play-calling has been way too predictable.
opinion.m: Blaming the offensive coordinator is a fan tradition.

opinion.t: Everything starts with the quarterback in this league.
opinion.m: A safe NFL truism. Nobody disagrees.

opinion.t: Defense wins championships. I don't care what anybody says.
opinion.m: An old saying. Works best after a low-scoring game.

agree.m: Safe for any take, good or bad.
Makes it sound like you had the take first.
They're mid-rant. Let them keep going.
For any complaint about your own team.
Shared misery after a bad game.
Firm agreement without adding anything you'd have to back up.

dodge.m: Anyone can beat anyone. Ends a debate.

dodge.t: I'll believe it when I see it.
dodge.m: Someone predicts big things. Doubt sounds wise.

dodge.t: Depends which version of us shows up.
dodge.m: Works for any team, because every team is inconsistent.

dodge.t: I stopped making predictions with this team a long time ago.
dodge.m: Sounds like a fan who's been burned before.

dodge.t: Ask me again in a couple of weeks.
dodge.m: Buys time when someone wants a prediction.

dodge.t: Honestly, I just want them to stay healthy.
dodge.m: Nobody can argue with it, and it ends the question.

dodge.t: Lot of football left to play.
dodge.m: Any time before the playoffs. Sounds patient and wise.

dodge.t: Above my pay grade. I just yell at the TV.
dodge.m: When it gets technical. Gets a laugh and moves things on.

telly.m: A call that should have gone your way and didn't.
Your team keeps throwing and it isn't working.
Your quarterback is holding the ball too long and about to get sacked.
Your defense just missed another tackle.
A dropped pass. Hands on head.
Final seconds, clock running, no timeouts left. Spiking the ball stops the clock.
Your player breaks into the open field.
A close call went against you and the replay looks good for your side.

exit.t: Alright, I gotta run. Enjoy the game.
exit.m: Before or during a game day.

exit.t: Anyway, we'll see what happens this week.
exit.m: Noncommittal. Works whatever happened last time.

exit.t: I'll text you during the game.
exit.m: With a friend. Promises you'll be watching.

exit.t: Let's hope they figure it out. Catch you later.
exit.m: After any game that wasn't perfect, which is most of them.

exit.t: I need another beer. Good talk, man.
exit.m: At the bar. Nobody questions it.

exit.t: Gotta go, but we'll talk after the game.
exit.m: Before kickoff. Postpones the hard questions.

win.open: Solid win {when}. Took care of business.
win.them: Nice to have a stress-free one for a change.
win.back: That's how you do it. Show up, handle it, go home.
win.exit: One week at a time. Catch you later.

bigWin.them: That's what I like to see. Statement win.
bigWin.back: Just hope they don't get comfortable. Gotta do it again next week.
bigWin.exit: Enjoy it while it lasts. Talk soon.

narrowWin.open: That game {when} took a year off my life.
narrowWin.them: {score}. Way closer than it needed to be.
narrowWin.back: We'll take it. Ugly wins count the same in the standings.
narrowWin.exit: I need a calmer one next week. See ya.

tie.open: A tie {when}. {score}. I don't even know how to feel.
tie.them: Honestly, a tie feels worse than a loss.
tie.back: Ten minutes of overtime and nobody could finish it off. Brutal.
tie.exit: Well, at least it's not in the loss column. Later.

loss.them: Yeah, we just couldn't get anything going.
loss.back: Too many penalties, too many drives stalling out. Same old story.
loss.exit: Burn the tape and move on. Catch you later.

bigLoss.open: Please tell me you didn't watch {team} {when}.
bigLoss.them: I did. {score}. I want those three hours back.
bigLoss.back: We got pushed around in the trenches from the first snap.
bigLoss.exit: On to the next one. I'm not talking about this game again.

otWin.open: Overtime {when}! Did you see the finish?
otWin.them: I was up off the couch the whole time.
otWin.back: {player} came up huge when it mattered. My nerves are shot.
otWin.exit: That's why you watch till the end. Catch you later.

otLoss.back: Never should've gone to overtime. We had our chances.
otLoss.agree: Yeah, we left points out there.

comeback.open: How about that comeback {when}? We were down going into the fourth!
comeback.them: I almost changed the channel, honestly.
comeback.back: Never count this team out. Completely different team in the fourth quarter.
comeback.agree: It's never over till it's over.
comeback.exit: Hope they don't make me sweat like that again. See ya.

blewLead.open: We were up going into the fourth {when}. How do you lose that?
blewLead.them: Went into prevent and let them march right down the field.
blewLead.back: Every time. Play to win, don't play not to lose.
blewLead.exit: I'm turning games off after three quarters from now on. Later.

qbBigGame.open: {player} was cooking {when}. Did you see that?
qbBigGame.them: He was throwing dimes all day.
qbBigGame.back: Give him time in the pocket and nobody can stop him.
qbBigGame.exit: Keep that up and we're dangerous. Catch you later.

runGame.them: They couldn't tackle him. The line was opening up huge holes.
runGame.back: Old-school ground and pound. When we run it like that, we're tough to beat.
runGame.exit: Run it till they stop it. See ya.

defenseWin.open: That defense, man. Did you see {team} {when}?
defenseWin.back: Offense did just enough. Defense won that game.
defenseWin.exit: I'll take that every week. Later.

turnoverLoss.open: You can't throw picks like that and expect to win.
turnoverLoss.them: Brutal {when}. We kept giving them the ball back.
turnoverLoss.back: Exactly. Give a good team short fields and they'll make you pay.
turnoverLoss.exit: Hopefully they spend all week on it. Catch you later.

rivalWin.open: We beat {opp} {when}. Best day of the year.
rivalWin.back: {score}, and I finally get some peace in the group chat.
rivalWin.exit: I'm wearing my jersey all week. Later.

rivalLoss.open: Losing to {opp} {when}. Worst feeling there is.
rivalLoss.them: Their fans are gonna be unbearable.
rivalLoss.back: Already got texts from my buddies who cheer for {opp}. I'm muting the group chat.
rivalLoss.exit: We'll get 'em next time. Talk soon.

pub.say: Can you believe they kicked a field goal on fourth and one?
o: Gotta go for it there. Way too conservative.
Fans almost always want to go for it on fourth and short.
The win-probability models usually favor going for it in that spot.
Probably true, but it sounds like a spreadsheet.
At least they scored a goal.
It's a field goal, and nobody calls it just a goal.

pub.say: Our O-line got pushed around all night.
o: Their pressure rate allowed must be near the bottom of the league.
Right idea, but nobody talks in rates at the bar.
You lose in the trenches, you lose the game.
Line play is always the right thing to blame.
Which ones are the O-line again?
The big guys up front. Every fan knows that.
Brutal. You just can't throw that ball.
Short, pained and right.
Pick six? Like the lottery?
A pick-six is an interception run back for a touchdown.
Interceptions returned for scores are some of the costliest plays in the game.
Accurate, but it sounds like a textbook.

pub.say: The refs are throwing laundry all over the place tonight.
o: Why would they bring laundry to a game?
Laundry means penalty flags. Now he's explaining it to you.
Flag counts vary quite a bit from one officiating crew to the next.
Interesting, and completely the wrong mood.
Seriously. Just let them play!
Complaining about the refs is always welcome.
Don't ask. My kicker's outscoring my running backs.
Complaining about fantasy is exactly the right answer.
I set my lineup using projected points and matchup data.
That's how people do it, but nobody wants to hear it.
Fantasy? Like dragons?
Fantasy football. Most fans play it.

pub.say: Third and one and they throw it deep. Why?
o: Is third down the last one?
The NFL has four downs. Three downs is the CFL.
Just run the ball! Pound it in there!
On short yardage, fans want the run.
Defenses often sell out against the run there, so a deep shot can be the smart call.
Maybe right, but it sounds like you're defending the coach.

pub.say: You coming to the tailgate Sunday?
o: Wouldn't miss it. I'll bring the wings.
Food and enthusiasm. Perfect.
Sure, although I'm mostly interested in the tactical matchup.
Nobody goes to a tailgate for tactics.
What's a tailgate?
It's the pre-game party in the stadium parking lot. Everyone knows.

pub.say: Our defense bends but doesn't break.
o: Their red-zone touchdown rate allowed is genuinely elite.
True or not, that's a stat, not a chat.
Bends? Is that a stretching thing?
It means giving up yards but not touchdowns.
Give up yards, not points. I'll take it.
Shows you know exactly what the phrase means.

avoid.why: Football has touchdowns and field goals. Nobody says just 'goal.'
A touchdown is six points. The single point is the kick after.
Innings are baseball. Football has four quarters.
'Full-time' is soccer talk. Football fans ask for the final.
It's a field in North America. 'Pitch' gives you away instantly.
In the US and Canada it's just football. Soccer is soccer.
Fans have heard the rugby line a thousand times and hate it.

avoid.say: Who's in the Super Bowl final?
avoid.why: The Super Bowl is the final. Adding 'final' sounds foreign.
With a city name, North Americans say 'is.' 'The Packers are' is fine.
NFL midfield is the 50. The 55 was the CFL's, and even that goes in 2027.

nerd: Actually, once you strip out garbage time, his EPA per dropback on early downs is top five, and his completion percentage over expected backs it up.
offq: Wait, are they running a 3-4 or a 4-3 this year?
unsure: house call: only spam-quality sources use it for a touchdown, so left out. 'Take it to the house' / 'housed it' are confirmed instead.
throwing a duck: Under Armour defines it as a soft, easy-to-catch pass, which clashes with common use (a wobbly, ugly throw). Left out.
ballgame: not listed as a baseball giveaway, because football fans and broadcasters genuinely say 'ballgame' too.
CFL 'no yards' penalty: sources disagree on the current yardage, so left out.
two-and-out: confirmed from CFL team and media usage, not from an official glossary.
rouge: rules changed for 2026 (no single for a missed field goal that goes wide or a kick that leaves the end zone untouched). Still awarded when a kick settles in the end zone and isn't run out.
CFL field: 110 yards with the 55-yard line through the 2026 season; 100 yards with 15-yard end zones from 2027.

Pro Football Reference glossary and Merriam-Webster pages refused automated fetches (403); Merriam-Webster definitions were taken from search summaries. ESPN, The Athletic and CBS were not fetched directly.
Placeholders: the app fills {team} and {opp} with names like 'the Bears', so lines avoid 'the {team}', 'Go {team}' and a verb straight after a team name.
Tie exchange mentions ten minutes of overtime, which is the NFL regular-season rule (ties only happen there). College games can't tie.
